SMTO-HTTP-0006 — The service requires a client certificate

GUID: 0c4d7918-bf87-41b9-aee2-88b5eef7a795
Slug: http-client-certificate-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • This service only accepts connections that present their own security certificate, and this HTTP Connection doesn't have a working one set up. Your request wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Get the client certificate and its private key for this service from the service's administrator. Only the service's owner can issue a certificate it will accept.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select this HTTP Connection, and in TLS & transport set Client certificate to Certificate and key PEM and paste both, or to Files on Gateway and enter their paths. SMTO presents this certificate during the secure connection so the service knows who is calling.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. The test shows whether the service now accepts the certificate.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports Reachable and Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the service's administrator or the person who set up this HTTP Connection. Don't turn off TLS certificate verification; it won't satisfy the certificate requirement and makes the connection unsafe.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OAuth tls_client_auth is configured without a client certificate, or the TLS handshake failed with a certificate-required alert from the server.

What this means

  • OAuth client TLS authentication has no configured client certificate, or the TLS exception contains a certificate-required marker. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth client TLS authentication has no configured client certificate, or the TLS exception contains a certificate-required marker.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish the explicit OAuth requirement from the TLS marker and inspect the selected certificate/key configuration.

How to fix it

  • Configure the profile's client certificate and private key (Client certificate: Certificate and key PEM, or Files on Gateway with paths readable by the Gateway's account) and verify the server's trust chain or custom CA. Never disable certificate verification to work around this.
  • Configure the required client certificate and key through the supported profile; verify the server trust chain.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended client certificate/key pair is accepted through the configured trusted TLS connection.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
